content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] re: L/S "case study" if ur starting from scratch, there are models for practice in here, various formats no format is right or wrong per se the "right" format, is the one u can build from scratch in a blank template in 3-4 hours (IS/BS/CF) takes years to learn...so start now. --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] prob last & final statement on all things LLM/claude/modeling - sick of the topic if ur goal is to secure employment in L/S equity there is no path where u are not going to get roasted in an intvw, to see if you know financial statement analysis cold. theres no shortcut or backdoor there is no way to skate through the process or slip an LLM model by them at some point there will just be a round table, bunch of humans, no computers and if u arent fluent, its over firms will continue adding safeguards now that anyone can "one click" an excel model safeguards meaning: face-to-face evaluation of, "does this person know their shit or not?" there's no way around it if u are praying for some grand announcement "we now accept Claude," u are waiting for Godot aka: it aint happening when I was 23 I fought this shit like hell too, it sucks to learn, its boring eventually u realize there is no choice and u start dumping thousands of hours into practice thats why I say start now. because it will take u years, like, not one or two, but several, until u are proficient if u dont really want this career, u will give up if u do, u are going to do whatever the fuck it takes thats all folks in the words of sean connery: "losers whine about their best, winners go home and f*** the prom queen." if anything in there isn't clear, DM me.
